headings: Check a wallet before you pay it.

01-intro-why.copy:
WHY THIS EXISTS
The Lazarus Group
North Korea's state hackers. They have stolen billions in crypto and moved it through thousands of addresses. Paying one of those wallets, or one close to it, is the risk.

02-intro-demo.title: Lazarus Scan · Newton
headings: Check a wallet before you pay it.
A policy decides what to check.
02-intro-demo.copy:
WHAT THIS DEMO DOES
Check a wallet before you pay it.
Choose a policy, pick a wallet and run the check. The policy looks for a path from the wallet to a known Lazarus address, and Newton Protocol operators sign the result as an attestation anyone can check.

03-intro-policy.title: Lazarus Scan · Newton
headings: Check a wallet before you pay it.
A policy decides what to check.
03-intro-policy.copy:
PART 1 · THE CHECK
A policy decides what to check.
A policy is a rule plus the data it reads. Here the data is a wallet scanner built on a list of known Lazarus addresses, and the rule is how many hops count. Anyone can write a policy, with any data source.
Start with a policy
Next
Lazarus
1 hop
2 hops
3 hops
W
Wallet you pay
This policy covers 2 hops. The wallet at 3 is outside it.

04-intro-enforcement.title: Lazarus Scan · Newton
headings: Check a wallet before you pay it.
A policy decides what to check.
04-intro-enforcement.copy:
PART 2 · ENFORCEMENT
Newton enforces it.
Newton Protocol operators run the policy on the wallet you are about to pay, and a quorum signs the result. The signed result can't be altered, and anyone can check it on the explorer.
